newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Demonstrators mass in Belgrade square.
newsitem.headline: Demonstrators mass in Belgrade square.

text.p: Around 50,000 demonstrators massed in a Belgrade square on Sunday in the 42nd straight day of pro-democracy demonstrations in Yugoslavia.

Witnesses said Serbian security police, enforcing a ban on street marches after a December 24 riot between protesters and government loyalists, lined adjacent roadways as opposition leaders addressed the crowd.
Music blared from loudspeakers in Republic Square and the situation was reported calm.

Demonstrators, sometimes as many as 250,000, have taken to the streets daily since the ruling Socialist Party (SPS) annulled November 17 municipal elections won by the opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition.
Zajedno, backed later by findings of a special OSCE mission, accused the SPS of rampant vote-rigging and wants its victories reinstated in 14 large cities including Belgrade.

Major Western governments have warned Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic he will get no financial aid for Yugoslavia's wrecked economy unless he concedes SPS electoral defeats and undertakes democratic reforms.
